title: Restoring Integrity to America's Financial System

enrichment.summary: This executive order directs the Treasury and financial regulators to strengthen protections against financial fraud and abuse, particularly linked to unauthorized immigrants and illicit cross-border financial activities. It calls for improved customer identification, enhanced due diligence, and new guidance on managing credit risks associated with lending to non-work authorized populations to help restore trust and safety in the U.S. financial system.
potential_concerns: The enhanced due diligence and customer identification requirements may restrict undocumented immigrants and non-work authorized visa holders’ access to basic financial services, potentially pushing them toward unregulated financial alternatives.

Small business owners and agricultural workers employing non-work authorized individuals might face increased scrutiny and operational challenges due to intensified payroll tax enforcement and financial reporting standards.

The order may inadvertently exacerbate financial exclusion and economic vulnerability among low-income families who rely on informal or alternative banking methods due to lack of lawful immigration status.

Law enforcement agencies may experience increased workloads and challenges balancing national security goals with civil rights protections for immigrant populations under enhanced financial regulation.
Financial services workers will need to implement new complex compliance protocols rapidly, possibly straining resources and increasing operational costs for institutions serving diverse communities.
